newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 19.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Thursday.
- Labour delivered a dramatic double blow to four of its star ministers yesterday, passing them over for Senate nominations only a fortnight after they lost their Dail seats.

- Private charities are to be allocated five million Irish pounds a year from lottery cash as a new report recommends that the state stop using the funds to supplement Exchequer spending. - Economic growth surged to eight percent last year, finance minister Ruairi Quinn indicated yesterday.

- British prime minister Tony Blair is believed to be preparing a statement outlining his approach to future political developments in Northern Ireland in the aftermath of the IRA murder of two police officers.
- Figures out today are expected to show that the economy grew at a record pace last year.
- Minister for Education Niamh Breathnach has ruled out seeking a nomination elsewhere for the Senate elections following her surprise failure to be nominated by the Labour Party.
- Ten Fianna Fail places are as good as filled in Bertie Ahern's new cabinet but the remaining three places are oversubscribed.

- Canadian police and justice officials returned to Ireland yesterday amid fresh hopes of a breakthrough in the criminal investigation into the Air India disaster which claimed over 300 lives in 1985.
- The Loyalist ceasefire was in tatters last night after the UVF officially threatened to murder a senior prison governor in Northern Ireland.
